required_evidence: Construct from the finite-observation records a lower semicontinuous convex G with 0 <= G <= f, and prove that every h:E→[-∞,+∞] with closed convex real-height epigraph and h <= f satisfies h <= G, including competitors that take -∞.
Establish the relation between raw records when F is contained in K and connect the family of records to the resulting global G; any equivalent rigorous reconstruction is acceptable.
Justify the relevant extended-value operations and all invoked separation or duality theorems under the actual locally convex hypotheses.
critical_errors: Identify the resulting G with the original f solely from convexity.
Assume the fiber infima or global infimum are attained.
Assert that finite-dimensional projection preserves closed epigraphs, or that inf-projection commutes with relaxation without a justified closure step.
Use a finite-dimensional or normed-space-only theorem for arbitrary Hausdorff locally convex E without proving an applicable extension.
Construct an arbitrary minorant but omit the specified maximality or any connection to the finite records.
Restrict competitors to proper functions or silently apply a proper-only Fenchel–Moreau statement to an arbitrary h:E→[-∞,+∞] without a valid reduction covering the specified full class.
completion_policy: The maximality specification remains mandatory because it is the precise main goal, not a prescribed proof route. An affine dual formula, biconjugate notation, the optional refined record identity and author counterexamples are not separate requirements. A correct short reconstruction with the required record relations fully completes the case. The epigraph convention fixes the competitor class, not a mandatory proof route; a valid direct epigraph, separation, conjugacy, or reduction argument is accepted.
open_task_policy: Accept every independently verified proof or counterexample within the actual hypotheses. Do not require the author route, vocabulary, length, optional examples or conditional results. Explicit added-assumption results are valid separate contributions; silently treating them as completion of the original task is not. Honest incompleteness is distinct from an invalid proof.
